hook.text: The internet was designed to survive a nuclear attack. Destroy any node and traffic reroutes. That's resilience.

buildup.text: ARPANET's packet-switching design ensured no single point of failure. Messages find alternative paths automatically.

discovery.text: Network resilience depends on structure: redundant paths, decentralization, and diverse routing create robustness.

twist.text: Centralized networks fail catastrophically. Take out the hub and the entire network collapses—a single point of failure.

climax.text: Shannon's noisy channel theorem applies to networks: redundancy in routing lets information survive link failures.

punchline.text: Redundant paths keep networks alive. Centralization kills resilience.

quiz.question: Why is a decentralized network more resilient?
options: No single point of failure can bring it down
